question: Which stored halfwords does the later wonder eligibility gate read, and what exact values do the 37 initialized records contain?

scope.boundary: The outer gate is inspected after its accepted inner gate. This packet covers its generic branch and all three exact cells in initialized records. Wonder-outer-gate-special-19-20 owns the two special branches. Field writers, human-readable field meanings, other selection paths, and runtime effects remain outside this packet.

dependencies.use: Establishes the inner-gate call and early zero return.
Bounds the accepted initialized record domain at 200 through 236.
Establishes 0x830EDC48 as 48 technology ownership words, one bit per player, with acquisition and persistence owners.

genericBranch.condition: After a nonzero inner result, normalized indices 19 and 20 take separate branches. Other indices enter the generic branch at 0x82CF3740.
genericBranch.recordSelection: The generic branch computes 0x82F73238 + normalizedIndex * 0x14C without a local bounds check.
genericBranch.firstTwoCells: It sign-extends the halfwords at +0x44 and +0x46, passing each as argument one to 0x82CEF6A8 with the caller-supplied r4 selector as argument two. Either zero helper result returns zero from the outer gate.
genericBranch.helperLocalRule: 0x82CEF6A8 is the accepted ordinary technology ownership query. It returns one for sentinel input -1 and zero for input zero. For other technology IDs, a nonzero neutral condition 0x82CEF4E8(17,-1) accepts values other than 47; otherwise it tests the selected player's bit in technology ownership word 0x830EDC48 + technologyId*4.
genericBranch.thirdCell: The generic branch sign-extends +0x48. A value of -1 returns one. Otherwise it tests technology ownership word 0x830EDC48 + value*4 after masking out the selected player's bit; a nonzero remaining result returns zero and zero returns one.
genericBranch.qualification: The three cells index the accepted technology ownership array on this path. Their broader policy meaning, the neutral selector-17 condition, and a global valid-ID predicate remain unresolved. The branch does not locally validate the record index.

recordValues.addressRule: For each row, each exact field address is 0x82F73238 + (itemId - 200)*0x14C + the listed offset.
recordValues.qualification: Values for 219 and 220 are stored facts; their special gate branches bypass the generic reads. Other cells are technology IDs or -1 sentinels on this exact branch; their effects are not inferred from numerical resemblance.

runtimeObservation.result: One fresh-game run logged zero inner-gate results for indices 0 through 32. This does not show execution of the outer generic branch after a nonzero inner result.

currentEvidence.method: A narrow exact-function generated-code window localized the generic branch and helper. Two foreground read-only canonical-project raw-word queries checked their branch instructions. One 37-position word query read exactly +0x40, +0x44, and +0x48 words per accepted record, from which the three signed halfwords were decoded.

entries.result: Indexed +0x44, +0x46, and +0x48 halfword loads, two helper calls, and final bitset condition.
Minus-one and zero cases, condition 17, value 47, and selector bitset read.
Three exact signed halfwords decoded for each of 37 accepted records.

currentEvidence.qualification: The configured decompiler truncates the outer function at a save thunk and the helper at bad instruction data. Current-image raw words support the branch and cells; generated code only corroborates decoded instruction meaning.

guards: Do not turn the technology ownership checks into a complete wonder buildability or effect rule.
Do not apply this branch to normalized indices 19 or 20 or treat its unchecked arithmetic as validation.
Do not infer runtime branch activation, buildability, completion, or gameplay effects from stored values.
conclusion: The outer gate consumes three signed halfwords at wonder-record offsets +0x44, +0x46, and +0x48 for its generic branch. The first two pass technology IDs or -1 sentinels to the accepted ordinary ownership query; the third tests whether other players own a selected technology. Exact values are mapped for initialized IDs 200 through 236. The branch has no local range check; wonder-outer-gate-special-19-20 owns the two special branches. Complete eligibility and runtime effects remain unresolved.
